exposure: Extremely preterm birth (<28 weeks gestational age) at term equivalent age vs. healthy term birth
outcome: Oxygen saturation profile (percentage of time spent below 90% saturation)
cohort: The study included 15 extremely preterm infants (born <28 weeks, very low birthweight) evaluated at term equivalent age before discharge, and 15 healthy term newborns evaluated after 48 hours of life.
finding: Term equivalent preterm infants spent significantly more time with oxygen saturation below 90% compared to healthy term infants, and feeding had little effect on the saturation profile within each group.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken when preterm infants reached term equivalent age (before discharge) and when term infants were after 48 hours of life.
birth_weight: Very low birthweight (<1500g) for the preterm group; not specified for term infants.
gest_age: Less than 28 weeks for preterm infants; term (37+ weeks) for the comparison group.
